panels.title: Five systems, one copy of the truth

panels.title: The churn model
panels.body: One model, registered in Unity Catalog with the alias champion, scores every eligible subscriber from viewing quality, payment and engagement features.

panels.title: Monitored, and retrained by rule
panels.body: After every scoring run, a monitoring job compares accuracy on the latest labelled month with accuracy at training, and measures drift (PSI) on the model's top features between the training months and the post-game snapshot. When the rule trips, a challenger is trained and replaces the champion only if it scores better on the same held-out month.

panels.title: Learning from outcomes
panels.body: Save rates come from past holdout tests (treated minus holdout), with an 80% range. Every new test the plan runs is added to the same table, so the next plan is sized from what actually worked.

panels.title: A different message for every subscriber
panels.body: ai_query writes one message per at-risk subscriber in a single batch through Unity Gateway. Personal data is masked and kids profiles are filtered before the model sees anything. Regenerate writes a new one live, with the same prompt and rules.

panels.title: Served from Lakebase
panels.body: Churn scores and messages are synced from Unity Catalog into Lakebase, the Postgres database the app and support tools read one subscriber at a time, in milliseconds. Each card shows its subscriber's live row.

panels.title: Approval, then action
panels.body: Nothing is sent until a person approves. The approval is written to an app-owned table in Lakebase.

data.summary: You want to see how many Sports cancellations occurred on February 15, 2027, compared to the expected number of cancellations for that day. On **2027-02-15**, **Sports** had **15,800** governed cancellations, with reconciliation status **within_tolerance**.
data.sql_text:
WITH `sports_cancels` AS (
  SELECT
    `day`,
    `tier`,
    MEASURE(`cancels`) AS `governed_cancels`
  FROM `cindy_wu_catalog`.`streamco`.`mv_streamco_metrics`
  WHERE `day` = DATE'2027-02-15'
    AND `tier` = 'Sports'
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT
  r.`day`,
  r.`tier`,
  s.`governed_cancels`,
  r.`subscriber_live_cancels`,
  r.`ledger_cancels`,
  r.`pct_diff`,
  r.`status`,
  r.`likely_cause`,
  e.`yhat` AS `expected_cancels`,
  e.`lo` AS `expected_lo`,
  e.`hi` AS `expected_hi`,
  e.`actual` AS `expected_table_actual`,
  e.`outside_band`
FROM `cindy_wu_catalog`.`streamco`.`gold_reconciliation_daily` r
LEFT JOIN `sports_cancels` s
  ON r.`day` = s.`day` AND r.`tier` = s.`tier`
LEFT JOIN `cindy_wu_catalog`.`streamco`.`gold_cancel_expected` e
  ON r.`day` = e.`day` AND r.`tier` = e.`tier`
WHERE r.`day` = DATE'2027-02-15'
  AND r.`tier` = 'Sports'

data.question: Why did Sports cancellations jump after the game?
data.headline: Nearly two-thirds of the extra cancellations trace to the same 20 minutes of halftime.
data.narrative: Sports recorded 15,800 cancellations versus 8,977 expected. Of the excess, playback issues accounted for 2,302 cancellations (33.7%), event-only churn for 2,064 (30.3%), payment failures for 1,999 (29.3%), and unexplained causes for 458 (6.7%). The “Payment retry policy” says declined sign-ups are retried once after 1 hour, but processor timeouts were excluded from retries and instead cancelled when the 24-hour grace window expired. In addition, 965 Sports support conversations said customers were charged, declined and cancelled. The Finance ledger recorded 15,760 cancellations versus 15,800 observed, a 0.25% difference that was within tolerance.

subscriber_entity.sql: SELECT 'Subscriptions' AS system, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) AS subscriber_ids, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) - count(DISTINCT a.subscriber_id) AS unmatched_ids FROM silver_subscription_events x LEFT JOIN silver_accounts a ON a.subscriber_id = x.subscriber_id UNION ALL SELECT 'Billing' AS system, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) AS subscriber_ids, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) - count(DISTINCT a.subscriber_id) AS unmatched_ids FROM silver_billing_attempts x LEFT JOIN silver_accounts a ON a.subscriber_id = x.subscriber_id UNION ALL SELECT 'Support' AS system, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) AS subscriber_ids, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) - count(DISTINCT a.subscriber_id) AS unmatched_ids FROM silver_support_cases x LEFT JOIN silver_accounts a ON a.subscriber_id = x.subscriber_id UNION ALL SELECT 'Payments' AS system, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) AS subscriber_ids, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) - count(DISTINCT a.subscriber_id) AS unmatched_ids FROM silver_processor_events x LEFT JOIN silver_accounts a ON a.subscriber_id = x.subscriber_id UNION ALL SELECT 'Telemetry' AS system, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) AS subscriber_ids, count(DISTINCT x.subscriber_id) - count(DISTINCT a.subscriber_id) AS unmatched_ids FROM silver_sessions x LEFT JOIN silver_accounts a ON a.subscriber_id = x.subscriber_id

data_quality.label: Data quality rules, latest full pipeline runs
data_quality.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT * FROM event_log(TABLE(cindy_wu_catalog.streamco.silver_accounts)) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM event_log(TABLE(cindy_wu_catalog.streamco.gold_cancel_events))), upd AS (SELECT origin.pipeline_name AS pipeline, max_by(origin.update_id, timestamp) AS update_id, max(timestamp) AS run_ts FROM ev WHERE event_type = 'create_update' AND details:create_update.full_refresh::boolean GROUP BY 1), cur AS (SELECT ev.*, upd.pipeline, upd.run_ts FROM ev JOIN upd ON ev.origin.update_id = upd.update_id), res AS (SELECT pipeline, explode(from_json(details:flow_progress.data_quality.expectations, 'ARRAY<STRUCT<name: STRING, dataset: STRING, passed_records: BIGINT, failed_records: BIGINT>>')) AS e FROM cur WHERE event_type = 'flow_progress' AND details:flow_progress.status = 'COMPLETED'), act AS (SELECT DISTINCT a.name, a.action FROM (SELECT explode(from_json(details:dataset_definition.expectations, 'ARRAY<STRUCT<name: STRING, action: STRING>>')) AS a FROM cur WHERE event_type = 'dataset_definition')) SELECT u.pipeline, res.e.name AS rule, regexp_replace(res.e.dataset, '^.*[.]', '') AS dataset, act.action, res.e.passed_records AS passed, res.e.failed_records AS failed, u.run_ts FROM upd u LEFT JOIN res ON res.pipeline = u.pipeline LEFT JOIN act ON act.name = res.e.name ORDER BY u.pipeline DESC, failed DESC, rule

model_monitoring.label: Churn model drift: training vs the post-game snapshot
model_monitoring.sql: SELECT label, feature, importance_rank, is_top, psi, baseline_mean, current_mean, drift FROM churn_monitoring_features ORDER BY is_top DESC, psi DESC

save_rate_sources.label: The past holdout tests behind each save rate
save_rate_sources.sql: SELECT card_id, test_id, run_date, n_treated, n_holdout, treated_rate, holdout_rate, lift, card_save_rate_from_tests, plan_save_rate FROM churn_monitoring_outcomes ORDER BY card_id, run_date
